If you only care about split times, get a Concept2 RowErg. If you want instructors filmed on real water, get a Hydrow.


Garage Gym Reviews named the[Aviron Strong Series Rower](https://www.avironactive.com/shop/strong-series-rower/) its[Best Overall High-End Rowing Machine](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/the-best-rowing-machine) for 2026. Full disclosure: Aviron makes the Strong Series, and we'll say plainly where another rower is the better buy. Competitor details come from each brand's US website, checked in November 2026. We've left prices out because they change too often to stay accurate.

## What Makes a Rower the Best?


Most rowers in 2026 are well built, so the differences come down to four things.


### 1. Resistance you can change mid-row


Air rowers like the Concept2 get harder the faster you pull, which feels natural but gets loud. Magnetic resistance is the quietest. Water sounds lovely, but on most water rowers you can't change the load mid-workout. The Strong Series combines air and magnetic resistance across 16 levels, from about 1 to 100 lb, and runs at about 60 dB, roughly the level of a normal conversation. More in[how loud is a rowing machine?](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/how-loud-is-a-rowing-machine/)


### 2. A fit for your body


Check three numbers: the weight limit, the tallest user the rail fits, and the seat height. A 20-inch seat like Aviron's is far easier to get on and off than the 11 to 16-inch seats on most rowers, especially if you're tall or have stiff knees.


### 3. Footprint and storage


Rowers run about 7 to 8 feet long in use, so look for one that stands upright on its own. The Strong Series is 84 inches long and stores upright with no wall mount. Hydrow needs an add-on kit to stand upright, and the Concept2 separates into two pieces instead.


### 4. Whether you'll still be using it


Spec sheets leave this out, but plenty of home rowers turn into an expensive clothes rack by month two, once the novelty wears off. That's the motivation cliff, and it isn't a willpower problem: most cardio machines were engineered to be boring, while the phone in your pocket was engineered to be hard to put down. So weigh the screen as seriously as the flywheel.


On the Strong Series, your stroke is the controller.

## Which Rower Is Best for Your Training Style?


The Strong Series isn't the right rower for everyone. For these buyers, we'd pick something else.


### Best for performance and racing: Concept2 RowErg


The Concept2 is the rowing world's benchmark. It's the rower in most CrossFit gyms, its PM5 monitor is the standard for logging splits, and it's very hard to break. It needs no subscription, but there's no content on the machine, the air fan gets loud at high effort, and the standard seat sits 14 inches off the floor. Already own one?[The Aviron app connects to the PM5](https://www.avironactive.com/aviron-app/concept2/) .


### Best for instructor-led rowing: Hydrow


Hydrow films its classes and scenic rows on real water, and its electromagnetic resistance is quiet. It comes in three models: Arc, Origin and Wave. The catch is that it has no games or streaming apps, tops out at 375 lb, and needs an add-on kit to store upright. Spec by spec:[Aviron vs Hydrow](https://www.avironactive.com/comparison/aviron-rower-vs-hydrow-rower/) .


### Best water rower: Ergatta


Ergatta's wooden water rowers look like furniture and run game-style interval workouts, with the Luxe rated to 500 lb and the Lite to 320. Water resistance rises with how hard you pull, but you can't dial it up or down mid-row, and the seat sits low, at 11 to 12 inches. Spec by spec:[Aviron vs Ergatta](https://www.avironactive.com/comparison/aviron-rower-vs-ergatta-rower/) .


### Best for iFIT households: NordicTrack RW900


If your treadmill or bike already runs on iFIT, the RW900 keeps you in the same app with the same trainers. It has a 24-inch pivoting touchscreen, 26 levels of magnetic resistance that iFIT can adjust for you, classes and scenic rows, Races and Meteor games powered by Ergatta, and streaming services. It's rated to 300 lb, doesn't fold, and needs an iFIT Pro membership for the full content.


### Best for Peloton households: Peloton Cross Training Row+


Peloton's rower brings the instructors and class style you know from the Bike and Tread, on a 23.8-inch screen that swivels. It stands upright against an included wall anchor and runs a few streaming apps, including YouTube and Disney+. It has no rowing games, though. It fits users up to 300 lb and 6'5", and Peloton content needs an All-Access Membership.


## Is a Smart Rower Worth It Over a Basic One?


Usually, if you use what's on the screen. A basic rower costs less up front, but the cost per workout depends on how often you row. Row three times a week for a year and that's about 150 workouts. Stop in month two and it's about 25. We ran the full numbers in[is a home rower worth it?](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/is-a-home-rower-worth-it/)


If you're self-driven and love chasing numbers, a basic rower is plenty. If you've quit a cardio machine before, put your money into the screen.


"I usually feel every second of misery on cardio machines... It's been almost three months and I've rowed at least five days each week without even realizing it."


Madie Moore, verified Aviron buyer

**Our verdict:** The Aviron Strong Series is the best rower of 2026 for most people. It fits almost every body, runs quietly, stores upright and is the only rower here that pairs a full game library with classes, scenic rows and streaming. Rowing purists should get a Concept2. ## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best rower to buy in 2026?


For most people, the Aviron Strong Series Rower. Garage Gym Reviews named it the Best Overall High-End Rowing Machine of 2026, and it pairs about 1 to 100 lb of resistance and a 507 lb capacity with games, classes, scenic rows and streaming. For a no-frills performance rower, the Concept2 RowErg is the classic pick.


### Which brand of rowing machine is considered the best?


It depends on what you value. Concept2 is the benchmark for training and racing, Hydrow for on-water instruction, and Ergatta for water rowing. Aviron leads on variety and on keeping people rowing: 92% of members are still working out a year later.


### What is the best rowing machine for beginners?


One that teaches you good form and gives you a reason to come back. The Strong Series has guided technique programs, a 20-inch seat that's easy to get on and off, and resistance that starts at about 1 lb. Our guide to[your first month of rowing](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/rowing-for-beginners-first-month/) covers what to expect.


### Which is better: an air, magnetic or water rower?


For most homes, magnetic or a combination of air and magnetic. Magnetic is the quietest and easiest to adjust, air feels natural but gets loud, and water sounds pleasant but usually can't be changed mid-row. The full breakdown is in[magnetic vs air rowers](https://www.avironactive.com/blog/magnetic-vs-air-rowers/) .


### Is 20 minutes of rowing a day enough?


For most people, yes. The[US Physical Activity Guidelines](https://odphp.health.gov/our-work/nutrition-physical-activity/physical-activity-guidelines/current-guidelines) call for 150 minutes of moderate activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week, and rowing hard counts as vigorous. Four 20-minute sessions at a hard effort cover it, and a steady 20 minutes most days gets you close.


### Do smart rowers need a subscription?


For classes and games, usually. The Strong Series still works without one for metrics-only rows and your streaming apps. Without a membership, Hydrow drops to a basic Just Row mode, and NordicTrack and Peloton need iFIT Pro or All-Access for their full content. Ergatta calls its membership optional but recommended, and the Concept2 needs none at all.


The best rower is the one you'll still use next year.
